correctness.rationale: For each p, failure when p∤b is exactly that the residue index t0=-a/b belongs to the first h_i places; after clipping at p, the union of forbidden initial segments has length max_i min(p,h_i). Primitive local pairs number p^2-1, leaving (p-1)(p+1-lambda) admissible. CRT and Möbius counting prove the fixed-tuple density. For generic inputs, only primes with p^p dividing at least one n_i matter; the small-quotient exceptions have density zero by bounded prime-factor counting. Prime-power CRT yields the all-order convergent Euler product. The strict covariance is proved by exact local identity p*(p^(-p))^2/(p+1)^2. Exact rational residue census, 6860 independent perfect-matching comparisons, and finite product diagnostics were rerun from the packaged verifier.

The accessible earlier single-input formula was recognized as covering k=1, which is excluded from the novelty claim. Searches for simultaneous and correlated divisor/progression matchings found no stronger equivalent. Residual historical-priority and easy-consequence risks remain and are expressly disclosed.
residual_risks: Historical completeness cannot be certified: equivalent simultaneous sieve computations may appear under another name.
A skeptic may regard the joint local-maximum identity as a short consequence of the 2026 pointwise criterion; the value claim rests on the natural correlated density problem and all-order law.
The existence theorem from arXiv:2610.37512 is invoked as a proved prior premise, without independently validating its entire proof.

value.rationale: The natural question of whether several divisor sets can be matched to progressions with the same start and step introduces genuine correlations. The full tuple local-maximum theorem is a structural complete classification, with nontrivial concrete boundary (4,8): 1/3 instead of the marginal product 2/9. Its all-order Euler product yields a computable, strictly positive common-environment covariance, extending single-input matching studies to correlated arithmetic data. The theorem makes no claim of a new matching existence criterion.
